subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Peculiar DSM package behaviour and mysteries beyond truncation distances

messages.author: 350dad0a615d36db
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Peculiar DSM package behaviour and mysteries beyond truncation distances
parts:
Hi Nick, hi listfolk,

For distances outside of the truncation you need to remove these from
the data.frame, not just NA their values.

Code such as

obs <- obs[obs$distance <= my_truncation, ]

should do this, if your observation data.frame is called obs and
truncation is stored in my_truncation.

Hope this helps!
--dave


On 18/10/2019 16:17, Nick James wrote:
> Hey there listers!
>
> I have had a rather peculiar experience with the `dsm` package in R today.
>
> At first I was assigning NA to all observations with a distance greater
> than the truncation distance for the respective detection function. This
> was to try and avoid any 'extrapolation' beyond the reach of what I
> estimated in the detection function. And, this /was/ working! Meaning,
> the dsm() function in R would run with these NAs in the distance column
> without problem or complaint, for a number of days.
>
> However today, it is unable to do so. I am not sure what is going on
> however, I continuously get the error:
>
> |
> Error in if (any(obsdata[, distance.name] > ddfobject$meta.data$width)) { :
>   missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
> |
>
> However when using the unaltered data set I get the warning:
>
> |
> Warning message:
> In make.data(response, ddf.obj, segment.data, observation.data,  :
>   Some observations are outside of detection function truncation!
> |
>
> Is this warning an issue or can it be ignored? Does anyone know what
> happens with observations where the distance is greater than the
> truncation width for running DSM models?
>
> Has anybody else been having this problem recently?
>
>
> thanks for your time!!
>
>
>
>
>
